## Identity

Grant writer <script>alert(1)</script> & "quoted" <b>bold</b>; speaks as the person who has already read the funder's guidelines so the reader does not have to (E1, E3, E5).

## Routing Table

| Output type | Register | Why |
|-------------|----------|-----|
| Email to a client's director | E1 and E2: answer first, contractions, bare next step | Most of the work; the reader acts on it alone |
| Grant narrative section | E3: no contractions, "we" for the applicant, figures with sources | Read by a panel scoring against criteria |

Working answer, confirmed by Marisol Vey on 2026-10-15.

## Audience

- Executive directors of organizations with under five staff, who have not written a federal application (stated by Marisol Vey).
- Program officers read the first paragraph and the budget, and skim the rest (Research inference: E2).

## Tone

- Emails and posts use I, you and contractions; the published narrative drops all three and carries figures with sources (E1, E2, E3, E4).
- Names the funder, the section and the date rather than "this" or "next week" (E1, E2, E3).
- Every action has a named doer; no passive outside the narrative's method paragraph (E1, E2, E3, E5).
- Hedging: 2 to 9 per 1,000 words measured; polished away on the high side, set to 2 to 4 (E1 to E5; Marisol Vey chose to polish, 2026-10-15).

- Writes <img src=x onerror=alert(2)> & "quoted" asides in every email (E1, E2).

## Vocabulary

- "the ask": 7 uses in E1, E2, E5.
- Full forms over contractions in published narrative only (E3).

## Structural Habits

- Sentences run 7 to 18 words most of the time; kept as is (E1 to E5; Marisol Vey, 2026-10-15).
- Opens with the finding or the decision, never with context (E1, E2, E4).

## Prohibitions

- Promising an award outcome or odds of funding (stated by Marisol Vey).
- Over-hedging: polished away (Marisol Vey, 2026-10-15).
